faqs.a:
(a)
Animal subject to a summons hold.
Any animal impounded by an animal management officer may be subject to a summons
               hold. An animal subject to a summons hold may be redeemed by and will be released
               to the owner or custodian if, within five days after the impoundment, the owner or
               custodian pays to the animal shelter the fees assessed by the shelter for costs related
               to the impoundment of, care of, and provision for the animal through and including
               the date of its release, if any, and accepts service of process as determined by the
               officer.
(b)
Animal subject to a court hold.
An animal that is being held pending municipal court proceedings for a violation
               of
section 14-51
, dangerous animals,
section 14-52
, aggressive animals, a third or subsequent violation within a one-year period by
               an owner or custodian of
section 14-54
, running at large,
section 14-91
, certain animals prohibited,
section 14-171
, cruelty,
section 14-171.5
, neglect,
section 14-174
, care of animals, or an animal belonging to or living within the same household as
               a person who has been adjudged to be a habitual offender under
section 14-11
may not be released except on order of a municipal court judge. The owner or custodian
               of the animal subject to a court hold may prevent disposition of the animal by the
               shelter if, within ten days after the impoundment, the owner or custodian:
(1)
Files with the court a payment in an amount determined to be sufficient by the animal
               management officer and the animal shelter to cover the costs of impoundment, care,
               and provision for the animal for at least 30 days including the day on which the animal
               was impounded, and continues to file these payments with the court as set forth in
section 14-206
(e)(1) throughout the pendency of the municipal court case; or
(2)
Files with the court a written petition for an impoundment hearing. The petition must
               state whether the owner or custodian is disputing probable cause for the impoundment,
               is disputing whether the costs of impoundment, care, or provision for the animal are
               fair, reasonable, and necessary, or both. If the owner or custodian does not indicate
               on the petition that they dispute probable cause for the impoundment, the owner or
               custodian will be presumed to have agreed that sufficient probable cause existed.
               If the owner or custodian does not indicate on the petition that they dispute the
               reasonableness of the costs of impoundment, care, or provision, the owner will be
               presumed to have accepted the stated costs as reasonable.
(i)
At the time the petition is filed with the court, the owner or custodian must also
               provide a copy of the petition for an impoundment hearing to the city prosecutor.
(ii)
If the owner requests a hearing under this section, the court must set the hearing
               to occur within seven days after the petition is filed.
(
Ord. No. 4878
, § 9, 10-7-2024)
